What I Learned From 50 Nairobi Parents About Raising Kids in the AI Era

Conversations with 50 Nairobi parents revealed five shared fears and three surprising hopes about children and AI.

Over six months, we spoke with 50 Nairobi parents, Karen, Westlands, Kilimani, Eastlands, Syokimau. Different incomes, different schools, same midnight searches.

Five fears dominated: inappropriate AI content, cheating, data privacy, lost critical thinking, and job prospects. Three hopes surprised us: parents want AI education, not AI avoidance. They want creation, not restriction. They want partners, not lectures.

A family AI policy template, simple rules everyone agrees on.

A place where children use AI with guidance, not in secret.

Other parents navigating the same confusion, community, not isolation.

AkiliNest was built from these conversations. The Parent Intelligence Series exists because parents asked for it.
